component.name: mongodb-gridfs
component.title: MongoDB GridFS
component.description: Store, read and remove files in a MongoDB GridFS bucket, and receive the files that are uploaded to it.
component.label: database,file

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelFileContentType.description: (producer) The content type that findOne read from the metadata of the file. (consumer) The content type of the file.

CamelFileLength.description: (producer) The size of the file that findOne found. (consumer) The size of the file.

CamelFileLastModified.description: (producer) The upload date of the file that findOne found. (consumer) The upload date of the file.

CamelFileName.description: (producer) The name of the file: the name that create gives the file, and the file that findOne, remove, listAll and count look for. (consumer) The name of the file that was found.

Content-Type.label: producer
Content-Type.description: The content type to store in the metadata of the file that create uploads. It replaces the contentType field of the CamelGridFsMetadata header.

CamelFileNameProduced.label: producer
CamelFileNameProduced.description: The name of the file that create uploaded, from the CamelFileName header.

CamelGridFsMetadata.description: (producer) The metadata to store with the file that create uploads, as a JSON document, and the metadata of the file that findOne found. (consumer) The metadata of the file as a JSON document.

CamelGridFsOperation.label: producer
CamelGridFsOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs when the operation option is not set: create, remove, findOne, listAll or count.

CamelGridFsChunkSize.label: producer
CamelGridFsChunkSize.description: The size in bytes of the chunks of the file that create uploads. If not set, or not greater than 0, the chunk size of the bucket is used, which is 255 KiB by default.

CamelGridFsFileId.label: producer
CamelGridFsFileId.description: The ObjectId of the file that create uploaded.

CamelGridFsObjectId.label: producer
CamelGridFsObjectId.description: The ObjectId of the file. create sets it to the id of the file it uploaded, and remove deletes the file with this id. If it is not set, remove deletes the first file it finds with the name in the CamelFileName header.

consumerOut.description: One message per new file: a stream of the content of the file (the stream cache when stream caching is on), closed when the exchange is done, with its name, length, upload date, content type and metadata in headers

producerIn.description: The content of the file that create, the default operation, uploads under the name in the CamelFileName header: text, bytes, a stream or a file. A Map, a POJO or no body fail. The other operations do not use the body; the CamelGridFsOperation header sets the operation when the option is not set

producerOut.description: create, the default, leaves the body unchanged, with the id of the file in the CamelGridFsFileId header. findOne gives a stream of the content of the file named by CamelFileName; listAll a Reader of text, one line per file with its name and id (the hex string of an ObjectId) separated by a tab; count the number of files as a Long; remove leaves the body unchanged

connectionBean.description: The name of the com.mongodb.client.MongoClient bean in the registry that connects to MongoDB. The endpoint closes this client when it shuts down.

bucket.description: The name of the GridFS bucket. GridFS stores the files of the bucket in the two collections named after it with the suffixes .files and .chunks, such as fs.files and fs.chunks.

database.description: The name of the MongoDB database that holds the GridFS bucket, and the collection of the persistent timestamp of the consumer.

readPreference.description: The read preference for the reads of the endpoint, as a name that com.mongodb.ReadPreference.valueOf(String) accepts, such as primary, secondary or nearest. If not set, the read preference of the MongoClient is used.

writeConcern.description: The write concern for the writes of the endpoint, as the name of a constant of com.mongodb.WriteConcern. If not set, the write concern of the MongoClient is used.

delay.label: consumer
delay.description: The time in milliseconds from the end of one poll to the start of the next poll.

fileAttributeName.label: consumer
fileAttributeName.description: The name of the field that the strategies with a file attribute set in the document of a file: processing while the file is routed, and done after it. The consumer removes the field when the exchange fails, so that the next poll offers the file again.

initialDelay.label: consumer
initialDelay.description: The time in milliseconds from the start of the consumer to its first poll.

persistentTSCollection.label: consumer
persistentTSCollection.description: The name of the collection in the database that stores the timestamp of the PersistentTimestamp and PersistentTimestampAndFileAttribute strategies.

persistentTSObject.label: consumer
persistentTSObject.description: The value of the id field of the document that stores the timestamp in the collection of the persistentTSCollection option. Consumers that keep separate timestamps need different values.

query.label: consumer
query.description: A query document in JSON that the consumer combines with the query of the queryStrategy option, to route only the matching files. Its fields are those of the document of a file in the bucket, such as filename or metadata.type.

queryStrategy.label: consumer
queryStrategy.description: How the consumer finds the new files. TimeStamp routes the files uploaded after the consumer started or after the last file it routed, and PersistentTimestamp stores that timestamp in MongoDB, so that it survives a restart. FileAttribute routes the files that do not have the field of the fileAttributeName option, and the strategies ending in AndFileAttribute require both.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs: create (the default), remove, findOne, listAll or count. If this option is not set, the CamelGridFsOperation header chooses the operation; the header does not replace this option.
